messages:
alex: heads-up: our latest invoice shows eu-west3 H100 effective unit cost higher than our committed rate. looks like ~9% delta vs ew1. tagging @priya for billing check.
priya: can you paste the billing lines or csv snippet?
alex: sanitized extract:
```:project,region,machine,usage_hrs,cost_usd
redwood-serving,eu-west3,h100,1440,134,400.00
redwood-serving,eu-west1,h100,1440,123,840.00
```
priya: that gap implies ew3 hours were not matched to our committed use. our commitments are regional — did we recently change scope?
jon: we updated the scheduler affinity last week to spread batch into ew3 when ew1 is saturated. if ew3 didn't have reserved buckets, those shifted jobs might be on-demand.
sarah: quick check: are customer-facing queries affected or only background batch?
alex: initial trace shows only batch windows hit ew3. customer-facing traffic stayed in ew1.
mike: back-of-envelope: moving 180 H100-hours/day from on-demand ew3 to reserved ew1 saves roughly $2.5k/day. but we need to confirm latency and throughput tradeoffs.
priya: action plan: 1) audit commitment mappings to regions and confirm whether auto-apply failed (I'll take this, due EOD). 2) finance-bot generate 30-day regionized GPU spend diff (finance-bot, pls). 3) temporary scheduler rule to avoid placing non-spot batch in ew3 (jon).
jon: I'll drop a low-risk guard in the scheduler to block non-spot batch landing in ew3 for 48h. will also add telemetry to measure queueing impact.
finance-bot: report ready (normalized to committed-equivalent hours):
```:period_start=1770040000,period_end=1770120000
eu-west1:H100:reserved=1,032,000.00
eu-west3:H100:on-demand=1,206,000.00
delta=174,000.00
```
finance-bot: note: figures use billing currency conversion at run time; minor FX noise possible.
priya: thanks. I'll also call our cloud rep tomorrow to see if we can extend committed coverage to ew3 or buy a small top-up at committed units.
sarah: I'm checking traces for any experiments or runs that might break if we re-home batch. found 1 active experiment and acme-inc had a nightly job in ew3 but their real-time requests are in ew1.
mike: if guard causes throughput loss, consider converting some batch to spot in ew3 to keep capacity but cut costs. model compares: top-up vs traffic shift vs spot conversion.
alex: finance threshold: if this drift causes >10% margin erosion on EU Dedicated offering, escalate to leadership. current projected monthly impact if unchanged = +$195k (+~3.9% margin hit) per finance-bot.
priya: uploading model links to drive: https://redwood.internal/drive/ew3-commitment-rebalance (internal). will post numbers when done.
jon: deploying scheduler guard now. will report 2h after deploy with queue metrics and placement summary.
priya: audit in progress. if auto-apply missed ew3 for any committed SKU, we might need retro billing adjustments (filing ticket with cloud billing).
alex: thanks everyone. tentative low-friction route = scheduler guard + rep negotiation + 2-week small-ew3 top-up trial. reconvene tomorrow 11:00 to decide.
finance-bot: forecast updated with no-action baseline: projected monthly delta = +$195,000.
_notes: Thread about EU region GPU billing/commitment mismatch; contains short informal messages, code block snippets, and bot outputs as per agents.md rules.
